newsitem.title: USA: UN approves 42nd Iraq oil sale for 990,000 barrels.
newsitem.headline: UN approves 42nd Iraq oil sale for 990,000 barrels.

text.p: U.N. overseers have approved the 42nd oil contract for Iraq under the oil-for-food accord, giving the okay for a sale of some 990,000 barrels of oil over 90 days, a U.N. spokesman said Wednesday.
Terms of the contract call for lifting of 11,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil over 90 days. The contract buyer was not immediately revealed by the United Nations.

U.N. officials said the latest contract was one of two contracts that had been pending approval in previous days, held-up by a lack of documentation. The other contract held-up for further clarification remained pending, an official said.

The oil accord allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of crude over a renewable six-month period, which began December 10 and ends on June 7. Most of the oil sale proceeds will be used by Iraq to buy food and medicine for civilians suffering from sanctions slapped on Baghdad after it invaded Kuwait in August 1990.

According to United Nations data, the total amount of the previous 41 oil sales was 113.2 million barrels. Including the latest, and 42nd contract, the new volume level was pegged at 114.19 million barrels.
